_README: The one place src/shared/data/buffs.json is edited. tools/build-roster.js re-applies every
entry here on a rebuild, so a correction or addition survives instead of being lost.
Every entry needs a 'why' naming who verified it and how - so nobody has to guess later
whether a number was measured or assumed.
TO CORRECT AN EXISTING ENTRY:  "<exact spell name>": { "why": "...", "set": { <fields> } }
TO ADD A NEW SPELL:  "<exact spell name>": { "why": "...", "add": { "kind": "buff",
The client spell files fill in landingText / endedText / iconId / castSec when the spell exists
in spells_us.txt (it usually does). Any field you put in 'add' overrides that, so a spell not in
the client data at all can still be specified in full - include landingText/endedText verbatim.
Add "noGameLookup": true to skip the client match when the name collides with an unrelated spell.
TO MARK A SPELL AS LASTING FOREVER, add:  "set": { "infiniteDuration": true }
Search this file for infiniteDuration to see the ones already marked. It shows a tile with no
countdown that stays until the ended text arrives - for spells with no duration BECAUSE they
genuinely have none, as opposed to instants like nukes and heals that do not last at all.

Alacrity.why: The owner, 24 August 2026, measured live in-game: the roster gave 660s (11m), but the real base duration is 492s (8m12s) - confirmed by her stopwatching a cast with no AA/Exaltation bonus applied. The wrong base was compounding with the real AA+Exaltation multiplier (65% on her current settings) to show an 18-minute timer, which is correct math over a wrong number, not a scaling bug - see buffEngine.js's _scaledDuration and gotcha 25 in CLAUDE.md for the multiplier itself.

Yaulp.why: The owner, 20 August 2026: named as an example of a spell with no imported duration because it genuinely lasts until dispelled or zoned, not because it is instant.

Yaulp II.why: A rank of Yaulp - identical landing and ended text - so it gets the same treatment. Marking only the base spell would leave the rank the owner actually casts still broken.

Yaulp III.why: A rank of Yaulp, same as Yaulp II - identical landing and ended text, so it gets the same treatment for the same reason. Leaving a rank unmarked would mean the spell behaves differently depending on which one the player happens to have scribed.

Fury.why: The owner, 20 August 2026: named alongside Yaulp as an example of a genuinely unlimited-duration spell.

Rage.why: The owner, 27 August 2026: "rage is permanent, too" - named directly while reviewing the Buff Planner, alongside Fury. Same berserk family, same "Your frenzy fades." ended text.

Fleeting Fury.why: eq-tracker-f8, 31 August 2026, from the log: 210 "<name> simmers with fury." lines across two different people (Korv, Avenrae - one a melee, one a caster), ZERO "begins casting Fleeting Fury" anywhere, and Shara never casts it herself. On EQ Legends "simmers with fury" is a melee/weapon proc that reuses this shaman spell's flavor text - the roster's othersLandingSuffix maps to a spell nobody actually casts. noBurstAllyAttribution stops ONLY the burst-context ally path from crediting the proc to the player as a buff she cast on a groupmate; a genuine named cast still attributes normally.

_CANDIDATES: NOT marked, because nobody has confirmed them - listed so the next person does not have to
rediscover them. Frenzy shares Fury's exact ended text ("Your frenzy fades.") and is the same
berserk family, so it is very likely infinite too. The owner named Fury and Rage, not Frenzy, and
guessing on her behalf is how a confident wrong number gets into the roster.
The wider list worth reviewing: 31 roster entries have a landing text, no duration, and are NOT
nukes or heals. Armor of Protection, Barbcoat, Wolf Form, Shrink, Feign Death, Banshee Aura,
O'Keil's Levity, Melanie's Mellifluous Motion, Minor Familiar, Cassindra's Chorus of Clarity.
RECAST TIMES are mined from the game data and are RIGHT MOST OF THE TIME BUT NOT ALWAYS.
Two were checked in game: Yaulp mined 18s and is 18s; Promised Renewal mined 21.5s and is 18s.
So one in two of the spot checks was wrong. Anything that shows a recast countdown should be
treated as a good default that the player can correct, not as measured truth, and a correction
belongs here as "reuseSec" rather than being typed into the roster.

Promised Renewal.why: RECAST: the owner verified 18s in game on 2026-08-20; the game data mines as 21.5s, which is wrong for this spell. Yaulp mined as 18s and she confirms 18s, so the recast field is right in general and wrong here in particular - do not 'correct' it globally on the strength of this one. DURATION: the owner verified 15s in game on 2026-08-19. The imported value was 18s and the client data says 18s, so both sources are wrong for this spell on this server. It is also the only spell in category 'Delayed' and its effect is a Final Heal after a fuse - the 18s is the delay before the heal fires, not a buff duration, which is why it must not take the AA duration bonus either.

Mesmerize.why: Measured from the owner's own logs, and it agrees with her note-17 table (30/36/36/40) against the imported value of 24. 189 Mesmerize wear-off lines were split by whether an "awakened by" break line sat within 1s: 99 breaks, 90 natural expiries. The natural expiries have a hard ceiling at exactly 30s - 13 sit on 30, none above it - which is what a real duration looks like. The imported 24s is wrong. Ranks II/III/V cannot be checked the same way: the owner has never cast them in any log.

_STANCES_AND_INVOCATIONS: Backlog #20 / #21. The owner, 31 Aug 2026, supplied the names ("numbers don't matter, only
the names"). These are the EQ Legends multiclass stance / invocation system - character states,
not timed buffs, so infiniteDuration:true (a tile with no countdown, cleared when it changes).
Every log line for this system is templated, confirmed against the owner's own log across six
of them: "You assume a/an <x> stance." and "You begin reciting the <x> invocation.", where
<x> is the name with the trailing " Stance"/" Invocation" dropped and lowercased - NO -ing or
other transform in any confirmed case ("Empowering" only looks transformed because the owner
named it "Empowering Invocation", not "Empower"). The nine that were not seen firing in a
logged session are marked derived: true - same template, article picked by vowel sound. If a
specific one turns out wrong, correct that one line; the pattern itself is confirmed.
Persisting the ACTIVE stance/invocation across a restart (backlog #16) is done separately
(abilityGroups.js) - this is only the roster presence + detection text.
